text.p: Onshore gas producer Santos Ltd said on Monday it would maintain its focus on exploration, spending at least $150 million in calendar 1997 from A$130 million this year and A$88 million last year.
Managing director Ross Adler told a Securities Institute of Australia briefing that Santos would drill close to its 1996 target of 99 wells for the year.
This was up from 66 in 1995 and particularly reflected increased activity in the Cooper Basin of South Australia where it has six rigs operating, and the possibility of adding a seventh.
Adler said it was important that most of the expenditure was in basins that were already in production, mitigating against the possibility of high write-offs from failed programmes.
Expenditure in 1997 would be in excess of A$150 million "and possibly even more than that", he said.
Adler said gearing could spike up into the high 70s for a brief period in 1997, but would not rise above 80 percent.
The company aimed at gearing of about 50 percent, but the increase was due to the high level of project development.
"We're probably spending A$600 million plus in 1996 and 1997 on capital," he said.

This included development of the Stag field off Western Australia and the Elang field in the Timor Sea, as well as construction of gas plants in Queensland, for which the company had long-term contracts.
"The fact that we have such secure cash flow from the gas business makes it not overly risky," he said.
Adler said Santos was looking at the petroleum assets of WMC Ltd, which have been put up for sale, but noted that it was already involved in many of the company's Australian projects.
"I don't know whether we will bid for part or bid at all," he later told reporters.
Adler said Santos was moderately bullish on the oil price for the remainder of 1996/97, with likely volatility and price spikes due to supply shortages.
Santos had not hedged its oil sales for some time.
"We have benefited from rising prices over the last two or three years to the full extent," he said.
"We can't see any factors on the horizon that really endanger a price above US$20 for the next year," he added.
The oil price closed at US25.62 a barrel in New York on Friday, hovering near six-year highs.
